messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Inference Gateway (private-vpc-prod-us-west-2) seeing elevated 5xx rate (>12% over baseline) and timeouts from private customers. Alert group: gateway-5xx-high. Links: https://ops.redwood/gw-alerts/3187650000

oncall_sre_maya: - I’m on it. grabbing logs & perf metrics. paging netops and runtime.

eng_runtime_jordan: seeing similar spike in tokens_served errors, looks like many upstream connections are getting TCP RST/504s around same time window. throwing up a quick query now.

netops_ashley: which path? private-vpc-prod-us-west-2? any peering changes in last hour? I don’t see any recent route updates in control plane.

eng_sre_liam: @eng_runtime_jordan can you paste the failing request logs? Are we seeing SYN retransmits or idle connections?

eng_runtime_jordan: pastebin: ```
2026-03-14T13:12:02Z gw-proxy[pid=78]: upstream=10.8.4.23:443 conn_reset after 1s; client=10.0.5.12:53712
2026-03-14T13:12:03Z gw-proxy[pid=78]: upstream=10.8.4.25:443 timeout after 30s; client=10.0.7.34:45211
2026-03-14T13:12:05Z gw-proxy[pid=78]: upstream=10.8.4.23:443 connection refused; client=10.0.6.22:60210
```

eng_runtime_jordan: pattern: many upstream IPs in the private NAT pool failing to respond. I suspect NAT translation issues.

netops_ashley: Ok that aligns. I’m checking NAT gateway metrics — ephemeral port utilization, conntrack. one sec.

netops_ashley: nat-gw-3 ephemeral_ports_in_use=65230/65535, conntrack=high, tcp_retransmits increasing. We might be hitting ephemeral port depletion.

oncall_sre_maya: customer impact? @customer_ops_lina can you triage top affected customers and whether they see 5xx in their dashboards?

customer_ops_lina: 3 enterprise customers reporting timeouts on inference calls, high error rates. I’ve opened support threads and notified account owners. They’re seeing 502/504s. putting them on hold and will relay mitigations.

se_rebecca: Are these customers using Private Dedicated or Private VPC? I need to surface the difference for support.

customer_ops_lina: Private VPC (customer-managed peering) for two, third is on Redwood Private with our peering.

eng_sre_liam: quick mitigation thought: scale out NAT pool / add another NAT appliance, or temporarily fail traffic to public inference path for affected customers (if allowed) to reduce pressure. We should be careful with routing churn.

netops_ashley: adding a second NAT appliance is possible but will take ~6-8 minutes to provision and attach to the VPC. I can try to enlarge ephemeral port range on existing appliance if supported. Trying hotfix: echo 'increase-ports' | nc nat-control 5050

deploy-bot: job/nat-control/increase-ephemeral-range started by netops_ashley (job id: jc-318765-a2)

netops_ashley: command returned: ERROR: appliance firmware older than 2.4 - ephemeral range increase unsupported. provisioning standby now.

eng_runtime_jordan: can we reroute affected customers to a different gateway in another AZ/region that has capacity? route policy can do failover, need deploy approval.

oncall_sre_maya: @eng_runtime_jordan prepare config diff for immediate rollback + failover policy. I’ll coordinate with @deploy-bot for a staged rollout.

eng_runtime_jordan: config diff ready, short snippet: ```
route_policy {
  match customer in [cust-A, cust-B, cust-C]
  action failover to gateway-private-us-west-2b
}
```

oncall_sre_maya: @netops_ashley if you provision standby NAT, we can failover traffic for those three customers to a different gateway, reducing nat pressure. netops go ahead?

netops_ashley: standby nat provision in progress, ETA ~7m. I’ll also open a conntrack cleanup on current appliance to free stale entries: `conntrack -F --zone 2` (careful: will drop active connections).

eng_sre_liam: Do not flush conntrack for entire VPC yet — that will cause mass disconnects. Try targeted cleanup: `conntrack -D -s 10.8.4.0/24 -p tcp --state TIME_WAIT` to reclaim ports.

netops_ashley: running targeted cleanup now.

eng_runtime_jordan: seeing immediate drop in RSTs after targeted cleanup. 5xx rate dropping from 12.8% -> 4.3% over the last 60s.

customer_ops_lina: Customers report partial recovery, some requests successful again. ongoing monitoring.

oncall_sre_maya: good. netops complete standby nat provisioning?

netops_ashley: standby nat attached and synced. I’ve applied route failover for affected customers to gateway-private-us-west-2b.

deploy-bot: route-policy apply started (id: rp-318765-b7)

deploy-bot: route-policy apply succeeded (id: rp-318765-b7)

eng_runtime_jordan: traffic shifting. 5xx rate now ~1.1%. Latency normalized for failover recipients.

oncall_sre_maya: escalating root cause: ephemeral port exhaustion on NAT appliance (firmware limitation preventing dynamic port expansion) causing connection failures and 5xx propagation to Gateway. Action items: 1) Netops to replace/upgrade firmware on appliance; 2) Eng-runtime to add a soft-failover policy to route when NAT saturation metrics cross threshold; 3) Product to notify customers & update postmortem.

netops_ashley: creating follow-up ticket NAT-REF-318765 with remediation plan: firmware upgrade schedule + capacity increase + alert thresholds.

se_rebecca: I’ll prepare customer-facing summary for tomorrow and coordinate with @customer_ops_lina.

eng_sre_liam: PR for soft-failover guardrail queued: `protective-failover-318765` — will include canary rollout and rollback.

oncall_sre_maya: great job everyone. incident-bot: set incident status -> mitigated. leaving this thread open for root_cause_analysis. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident 3187650000 status updated: mitigated by targeted conntrack cleanup + NAT standby failover. Postmortem required within 72h.

customer_ops_lina: noting customers affected & times, will attach support threads to postmortem.

eng_runtime_jordan: logs preserved at s3://incidents/3187650000/raw-logs.tar.gz and perf graphs pinned.

oncall_sre_maya: last check — 5xx steady at 0.6% and stable for 10m. closing paging window. thanks all.
